clue.text: Host being mad forgoing introduction

indicators.note: forgoing an introduction means the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A host who has gone off their head skips the introductions at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Barmy, British slang for mad, loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a large crowd or multitude, especially an armed one, as in the heavenly host.

clue.text: View favourably a cricket club with record turnover initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A cricket club's finances look good thanks to a record turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record turnover' reads as a financial boast; the record is a disc and only the first letter of turnover is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to regard it with approval or agree to it.

clue.text: Nordic city invested in formal monuments

indicators.note: invested in means wrapped inside the following words, which hold the letters

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian city has put money into grand civic monuments.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmo is a major city in southern Sweden, across the strait from Copenhagen.

clue.text: Ban cars moving round rear of Greek eatery

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around another piece
moving suggests the letters are shifted about into new positions
rear of points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A Greek restaurant wants traffic banned from going round the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters of 'ban cars' wrap around the K that ends Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack bar is a small cafe serving light meals, a kind of eatery.

clue.text: Group consuming, say, mint drink

indicators.note: consuming means one piece swallows another inside it

parts.note: mint is an example of a herb, signalled by say

explanation.surface: A group of friends sipping a minty drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet is, in older and regional use, a cooling fruit drink, from the Turkish and Persian word for a beverage.

clue.text: Calendar a Frenchman retained in northerly waterway

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading from bottom to top
retained in means held inside the waterway

parts.note: a canal is an artificial waterway
M is the abbreviation for monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's calendar was kept on a canal boat heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: Canal is written upwards, and M for monsieur slips in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is an annual publication listing dates, tides and astronomical events, a kind of calendar.

clue.text: Director working by lathe haphazardly

indicators.note: haphazardly means in random order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of a workshop operates a lathe carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters; 'haphazardly' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Kathryn Bigelow is the American film-maker of The Hurt Locker, the first woman to win the Oscar for best director.

clue.text: Quiet fellows entering a club in shame

indicators.note: entering means going inside the next piece

explanation.surface: Some subdued men walk into a nightclub, embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: The club here is a bat, not a nightspot; the quiet fellows go inside it after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Abashment is a feeling of embarrassment or shame.

clue.text: Sportswoman in struggle nears semi, harbouring a resolve

indicators.note: harbouring means holding something inside
in struggle suggests letters thrashing about out of order

explanation.surface: A tennis player fighting hard as she reaches the semi-final shows real determination.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a match report; 'in struggle' is the anagram signal, and A WILL sits inside the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Serena Williams is the American tennis player who won twenty-three Grand Slam singles titles.

clue.text: Last character with energy very much a fanatic

parts.note: the final letter of the alphabet
E is the symbol for energy
joins the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: The final person in line has a great deal of energy and is very keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last character' means the last letter of the alphabet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is an extreme, uncompromising enthusiast, which is what a fanatic is.

clue.text: School left stage in race in clutches of old athlete

indicators.note: in the clutches of means held tightly inside

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the British middle-distance runner of the 1980s
a leg is one stage of a relay or race

explanation.surface: A school pupil left a relay stage only to be grabbed by a veteran runner.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe was a British Olympic champion runner, later Lord Coe.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is a school, especially one for higher or further education.

clue.text: Gas encountered — hydrogen and nitrogen in a mine with minute gone

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next part
gone means taken away from what precedes it

explanation.surface: Miners met hydrogen and nitrogen underground, a gas hazard.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing MIN from A MINE leaves just A and E, and the nitrogen goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the flammable gas known to miners as firedamp, the simplest hydrocarbon.

clue.text: Saw dog restrained by lead

indicators.note: restrained by means held inside the following piece

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover is a traditional dog's name

explanation.surface: Someone saw a dog held back on its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, and 'lead' like a leash; it is a noun meaning a saying, and the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, the same thing as a proverb.

clue.text: Heading west, note around river pale Arctic animal

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means reading right to left

parts.note: a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: around means one piece wraps another

explanation.surface: A pale Arctic creature heads west around a river, as noted.
explanation.walkthrough: The river goes inside the word for pale, after the note, and the whole is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is a small whale of Arctic waters, the male bearing a long spiral tusk.

clue.text: Cute toy absent sadly in aesthetic competition

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's cute toy is sadly missing from a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty contest is a competition judged on looks, so aesthetic is a fair description.

clue.text: Swedish soprano in minor part of record showing weak spot

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next part

parts.note: the B-side is the lesser track of a single
Jenny Lind, the nineteenth-century Swedish Nightingale

explanation.surface: A Swedish singer given a minor role on a record reveals a weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny Lind was a famous Swedish opera singer of the 1800s; the B-side is the flip side of a single.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind side is the direction in which someone cannot see, and so their area of vulnerability.

clue.text: One studying jobs?

parts.note: surface reading: a careers adviser or someone researching employment; setter's reading: a job is slang for a crime, such as a bank job

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jobs' suggests employment, but in criminal slang a job is a robbery, so the student of jobs is an expert on crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminology is the academic study of crime and offenders, and its practitioner studies such illicit jobs.

clue.text: Firms working to create secure place

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, twice for plural firms

explanation.surface: Companies operating to build a safe haven.
explanation.walkthrough: Firms is plural, so the company abbreviation appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is a protective silky case, figuratively a sheltered, safe environment.

clue.text: Enthusiastic response over holiday about to be discounted

indicators.note: discounted means left out of the reckoning, so letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Delight at a discounted holiday offer.
explanation.walkthrough: CA, short for circa, is taken out of the word for holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a burst of applause, an enthusiastic reaction from an audience.

clue.text: Protective garment on the whole

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a loose coat or suit worn over clothes

explanation.surface: Wearing protective clothing, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a workwear coat and also works as an adverb meaning in general or taken as a whole.

clue.text: Good man always supported by daughter held out

parts.note: aye is an old word for always, as in for aye

explanation.surface: A decent man who always had his daughter's backing kept going.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supported by' means the daughter sits below the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have lasted or endured, just as holding out means persisting.

clue.text: Mark surfaced ill-advisedly? Not altogether

indicators.note: not altogether means only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters within it

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the hyphenated one

explanation.surface: Someone came up for air rashly, perhaps not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in ill-advisedly is ignored when reading the letters through.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is the diacritical mark placed under a c, as in facade, to show it is soft.

clue.text: Decrease, perhaps, to become equal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as de-crease, to smooth away creases
second meaning: to level off or balance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Decrease' looks like reduce, but split as de-crease it means flatten wrinkles, and 'perhaps' flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to smooth a surface flat and for differences to level off into balance.

clue.text: Approve a special number to see ruminant

parts.note: to OK something is to approve it

explanation.surface: Signing off a special performance for visitors to see a grazing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a cud-chewing African mammal related to the giraffe, so a ruminant.

clue.text: Welsh politician in beginning snubbed Japanese art

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next part
snubbed puns on snub-nosed, cut short at the end

parts.note: Assembly Member of the Welsh Assembly

explanation.surface: A Welsh politician was snubbed at the start of a Japanese art event.
explanation.walkthrough: AM stood for Assembly Member, a member of the Welsh Assembly; the word for beginning loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese art of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: A holy man strangely avoiding hospital? That's irregular

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: a thing that is irregular

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged
avoiding means keeping away from, so a letter is left out

explanation.surface: A saint who oddly stays away from hospital is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is something that deviates from the norm, which is what something irregular does.

clue.text: Singer entertaining a child at certain times

indicators.note: entertaining means having guests in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: Seal, the British singer of Kiss from a Rose

explanation.surface: A pop star occasionally puts on a show for a child.
explanation.walkthrough: Seal is a British soul singer known by a single name.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasonal describes something that happens only during particular parts of the year.

clue.text: Unrestrained Irish wit, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is identified by its sound when spoken

parts.note: Oscar Wilde, the Dublin-born playwright famed for his epigrams

explanation.surface: An Irish joker who knows no bounds, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild means uncontrolled or unrestrained, as in wild behaviour.
